Question 1
Which of the following molecules are identical?
  • A) i, iii only
  • B) ii, iv only
  • C) i, iv only
  • D) i, ii, iv only
  • E) All are identical molecules
Show answer
Answer: E — All are identical molecules

None of the drawn carbons is a stereocentre (each carries two identical groups), so the wedges/dashes don’t create different molecules.

Question 2
Which two of the following compounds are identical?
  • A) i, ii
  • B) ii, iv
  • C) iii, iv
  • D) i, iii
  • E) i, iv
Show answer
Answer: B — ii, iv

Rotate/flip the rings: ii and iv have the same OH arrangement on the same carbons.

Question 3
How many stereoisomers are possible for the molecule shown below?
  • A) 1
  • B) 8
  • C) 6
  • D) 16
  • E) 32
Show answer
Answer: D — 16

Answer key: 16 (4 stereocentres → 2⁴). Note: if the C=N oxime geometry is also counted, you get 5 → 32.

Question 4
Which compounds are meso forms?
  • A) i, ii
  • B) i, iii
  • C) i, iv
  • D) iii, iv
Show answer
Answer: B — i, iii

i and iii have identical groups on top and bottom and the same groups on the same side → internal plane of symmetry → meso.

Question 5
The triple chemical bond is composed of:
  • A) Three sigma bonds
  • B) Two sigma bonds and one pi bond
  • C) One sigma bond and two pi bonds
  • D) One pi bond and two sigma bonds
  • E) Three pi bonds
Show answer
Answer: C — One sigma bond and two pi bonds

Triple bond = 1 σ + 2 π.

Question 6
Which of the following about all the possible stereoisomers of 2-amino-1-phenyl-1-butanol is correct?
  • A) One pair of enantiomers, one pair of diastereomers and one meso compound
  • B) Two pairs of enantiomers and one pair of diastereomers
  • C) Two pairs of diastereomers and two meso compounds
  • D) Two pairs of enantiomers and four pairs of diastereomers
Show answer
Answer: D — Two pairs of enantiomers and four pairs of diastereomers

2 different stereocentres → 2² = 4 stereoisomers = 2 enantiomer pairs; each isomer is a diastereomer of the 2 others of the other pair → 4 diastereomer pairs. No meso (ends are different).

Question 7
Choose the correct answer (lowest to highest order of priority):
  • A) CH(CH₃)₂ < CH₂CH₂CH₃ < CH₂CH₂CH₂Br < CH₂CH₂Cl
  • B) CH₂CH₂CH₃ < CH(CH₃)₂ < CH₂CH₂Cl < CH₂CH₂CH₂Br
  • C) CH(CH₃)₂ < CH₂CH₂CH₃ < CH₂CH₂Cl < CH₂CH₂CH₂Br
  • D) CH₂CH₂CH₃ < CH₂CH₂CH₂Br < CH₂CH₂Cl < CH(CH₃)₂
Show answer
Answer: D — CH₂CH₂CH₃ < CH₂CH₂CH₂Br < CH₂CH₂Cl < CH(CH₃)₂

1st atom all C: CH(CH₃)₂ has (C,C,H) → highest. Others (C,H,H) → go to 2nd atom: CH₂Cl (Cl) beats CH₂ (C). Then CH₂Br at the 3rd atom beats CH₃.

Question 8
What is/are the possible chemical products of reacting HCl with 1,3-butadiene?
  • A) 3-chloro-1-butene
  • B) 1-chloro-2-butene
  • C) 2-chloro-1-butene
  • D) A and B
  • E) B and C
Show answer
Answer: D — A and B (3-chloro-1-butene and 1-chloro-2-butene)

Conjugated diene + HX → 1,2-addition (3-chloro-1-butene) and 1,4-addition (1-chloro-2-butene).

Question 9
Which of the following compounds will react with a hot concentrated solution of KMnO₄ to give only ketone, carbon dioxide and water as products?
  • A) i
  • B) ii
  • C) iii
  • D) iv
  • E) i, iii, iv
Show answer
Answer: D — iv

Hot KMnO₄ cleaves C=C: ring carbon → ketone (cyclohexanone); =CH₂ → CO₂ + H₂O.

Question 10
Which is correct?
  • A) The boiling point for branched alkanes is higher than that of straight-chain alkanes.
  • B) The boiling point increases for both of them if we decrease the number of carbons.
  • C) The molecular formula of both alkanes and alkynes is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂.
  • D) Terminal alkynes are more weakly acidic than alkanes.
Show answer
Answer: D — Terminal alkynes are more weakly acidic than alkanes

Terminal alkyne C–H (sp) is more acidic than alkane C–H. A, B, C are false (branching lowers bp; bp increases with more carbons; alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂).

Question 11
Which of the alkene starting materials will undergo ozonolysis (O₃), with subsequent treatment with H₃O⁺ and H₂O₂, to give compound Z?
Show answer
Answer: C — C (1-methylcyclohexene)

Z = HOOC–(CH₂)₄–CO–CH₃ (6-oxoheptanoic acid): one chain with a ketone (C bearing CH₃) and an acid (C that had H, oxidised by H₂O₂). Ring opens → 1-methylcyclohexene.

Question 12
Name the following compound:
Show answer
Answer: 4-ethyl-2,3-dimethyl-1,4-pentadiene

Main chain through both C=C: CH₂=C(CH₃)–CH(CH₃)–C(CH₂CH₃)=CH₂.

Question 13
Which of the following structures is 1-ethynyl-2-isopropylcyclohexane?
Show answer
Answer: E — E

Ethynyl (–C≡CH) on C1 and isopropyl on the next carbon (C2).

Question 14
Which compound will react with a strong base like NaH to form a –ve carbon?
Show answer
Answer: C — C (terminal alkyne)

Only a terminal alkyne has an acidic ≡C–H → NaH removes it to give an acetylide (–ve carbon).

Question 15
Hydrogenation catalyzed by platinum catalyst forms which product?
Show answer
Answer: A — A

H₂/Pt adds both H atoms on the same face (syn addition) → both H on the same side.

Question 16
Predict the organic product with correct absolute configuration for the following reaction:
Show answer
Answer: B — B

Diels–Alder of a diene with an alkyne gives a 1,4-cyclohexadiene; CHO and CH₃ end up on a C=C (sp²) so they have no wedge/dash.

Question 17
The reaction of an alkene with 3-chloroperoxybenzoic acid only is an oxidation reaction:
  • A) without cleavage of the pi bond, to give an epoxide
  • B) without cleavage of the sigma bond, to give an epoxide
  • C) without cleavage of both the pi and sigma bonds, to give an epoxide
  • D) with cleavage of the sigma bond, to give a cis alcohol
  • E) with cleavage of both pi and sigma bonds, to give an epoxide
Show answer
Answer: B — Without cleavage of the sigma bond, to give an epoxide

mCPBA breaks only the π bond; the σ bond stays → epoxide.

Question 18
Baeyer’s test is for ………… and it involves the use of ……… to give decolourization of the ……… color and formation of a ……… precipitate.
  • A) alkene, cold alkaline KMnO₄, green color, purple MnO₂
  • B) alkane, cold alkaline KMnO₄, pinkish purple, brown MnO₂
  • C) alkene, cold alkaline OsO₄, pinkish purple, brown OsO₂
  • D) alkene, cold KMnO₄, pinkish purple, brown MnO₂
Show answer
Answer: D — alkene, cold KMnO₄, pinkish purple, brown MnO₂

Baeyer’s test: alkene decolourises purple KMnO₄ and gives a brown MnO₂ precipitate.

Question 19
Assign the absolute configuration (R) or (S) at carbons 2, 4 and 5:
Show answer
Answer: 2R, 4S, 5S

Assign priorities at each carbon (N / ring / substituents), then look with the lowest priority group away.

Question 20
The major product expected from the following reaction is:
Show answer
Answer: E — E (acetophenone)

Alkyne hydration (HgSO₄, H₂SO₄) → Markovnikov enol → tautomerises to a methyl ketone.

Question 21
The correct major organic product expected from the reaction shown below is:
Show answer
Answer: B — B (trans-2-methylcyclopentanol)

Hydroboration–oxidation: anti-Markovnikov, syn addition → OH on the less substituted carbon, trans to CH₃.

Question 22
Which of the following compounds is/are conjugated alkene(s)?
Show answer
Answer: iii only

Conjugated = C=C–C=C alternating (separated by one single bond). Only iii has its double bonds conjugated.

Question 23
Which IUPAC name matches the structure?
  • A) i and iii
  • B) ii and iv
  • C) ii and iii
  • D) i and iv
Show answer
Answer: A — i and iii

i: 2,3,6-trimethylheptane ✓ · iii: 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane ✓ (lowest numbers + alphabetical).

Question 24
Which of the following is the strongest base?
  • A) Ammonia
  • B) Dimethylamine
  • C) Aniline
  • D) 4-Nitroaniline
  • E) Phenol
Show answer
Answer: B — Dimethylamine

2° alkyl amine: two electron-donating alkyl groups → strongest base. Aniline/nitroaniline are weaker (resonance); phenol is not a base.

Question 25
Which one is the product of the following reaction (Et is ethyl)?
Show answer
Answer: B — B (ether, OEt)

Answer key: Williamson synthesis → ether. Note: with a 2° halide and the strong base NaOEt, elimination (C) can also compete in reality.

Question 26
The compound shown can be prepared from:
Show answer
Answer: D — CH₃MgBr + benzaldehyde, then H₃O⁺

Grignard adds CH₃ to the C=O of benzaldehyde → 1-phenylethanol (2° alcohol).

Question 27
Which of the following chemical compounds are epoxides?
  • A) Only 2 and 3
  • B) Only 2, 3 and 4
  • C) Only 2 and 3
  • D) Only 3 and 4
Show answer
Answer: D — Only 3 and 4

Epoxide = 3-membered ring with O. 1 is an open ether, 2 is a 5-membered ring (THF).

Question 28
What is the expected order of boiling points of the following compounds?
  • A) 3 > 2 > 1
  • B) 2 > 1 > 3
  • C) 2 > 3 > 1
  • D) 3 > 1 > 2
  • E) 1 > 3 > 2
Show answer
Answer: B — 2 > 1 > 3

Alcohol (H-bonding) > ketone (polar) > alkane (non-polar).

Question 29
What is the major organic product obtained from the following reaction?
  • A) I
  • B) II
  • C) III
  • D) IV
  • E) None of the above
Show answer
Answer: A — I

LiAlH₄ reduces –C≡N to –CH₂NH₂ (primary amine, one carbon longer chain).

Question 30
Which of the following compounds are tertiary amines?
i. (CH₃)₂CHN(CH₃)₂
ii. CH₂CH₂(CH₃)N(CH₂CH₃)
iii. CH₃CH₂CH₂NHCH₃
iv. CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CH₂NH₂
  • A) i, ii
  • B) ii, iii
  • C) iii, iv
  • D) ii, iv
  • E) ii, iii, iv
Show answer
Answer: A — i, ii

Tertiary amine: N bonded to 3 carbons. iii is 2°, iv is 1°.

Question 31
Which of the following will separate aniline from a solution of aniline in diethyl ether?

  • B) Aqueous HCl
  • C) Aqueous NaOH
  • D) Aqueous CH₃COONa
  • E) H₂O
Show answer
Answer: B — Aqueous HCl

Aniline (base) + HCl → water-soluble anilinium chloride → moves into the aqueous layer.

What is the major organic product obtained from the following reaction?
Show answer
Answer: C — C (bromobenzene)

NaNO₂/HCl → diazonium salt; H₃PO₂ replaces N₂⁺ by H → bromobenzene.

Name the following compound:

Answer: 4-methyl-3-penten-2-amine

Chain of 5 C including C=C; number to give NH₂ the lowest number (C2); C=C at C3, methyl at C4.

Show answer
Answer: A — A

Product = 2-methyl-3-hexanol. Split at the C–OH carbon: (1) (CH₃)₂CHMgBr + butanal ✓ · (3) CH₃CH₂CH₂MgBr + 2-methylpropanal ✓. 2 and 4 give different alcohols.

Show answer

Answer: B — 4-methyl-2-pentanol

NaBH₄ reduces a ketone → secondary alcohol (C=O → CH–OH). Alkanes/alkenes are not formed. (The drawing omits the methyl branch, but the idea is ketone → 2° alcohol.)

Extra 5 · Imine & N-derivatives (Q10, Q11, Batch 2022)
Show answer
Answer: Q10: C · Q11: B — Q10: C=N–CH₃ (imine) · Q11: hydrazone, amine, imine, oxime

1° amine + ketone (H⁺) → imine (C=N–R). C=N–NH₂ = hydrazone, C–NH₂ = amine, C=N–CH₃ = imine, C=N–OH = oxime.

Extra 6 · IUPAC name (Q8, Batch 2022)

Extra 7 · Geometric isomerism (Q4)
Show answer
Answer: C — 2,3-dimethyl-2-hexene

Extra 8 · Ozonolysis (Q14)
Show answer
Answer: A — i, iii only

Reductive ozonolysis cuts C=C into C=O; the =CH–CH₃ end becomes CH₃CHO. Only i and iii have =CH–CH₃.

Extra 9 · Alkanes & alkynes (Q7)
Which statement about alkanes and alkynes is correct?
  • A) Branched alkanes have higher boiling points than straight alkanes
  • B) In alkanes and alkynes the boiling point will decrease when increasing the number of carbons
  • C) The boat conformation is the most stable one in cyclohexane
  • D) The general formula for both alkanes and alkynes is CₙH₂ₙ₋₂
  • E) Terminal alkynes demonstrate weakly acidic property than alkanes
Show answer
Answer: E — Terminal alkynes are (weakly) more acidic than alkanes

A ✗ branching lowers bp · B ✗ bp increases with more C · C ✗ chair is the most stable · D ✗ alkanes are CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ · E ✓ sp C–H of a terminal alkyne is more acidic. (Same idea as midterm Q10.)

Extra 10 · Ether + HBr mechanism
What is the mechanism of this reaction?
  • 1- SN1
  • 2- SN2
  • 3- SN1 followed by SN1
  • 4- SN1 followed by SN2
Show answer
Answer: 1 — SN1

CH₃–O–CH(CH₃)₂ + HBr (1 mole) → CH₃OH + (CH₃)₂CHBr. Br attacks the R group that gives the more stable carbocation (2° isopropyl) → by the doctor’s rule, cleavage at a 2°/3° carbon = SN1. Only one mole of HBr → one step, so not “followed by”.

Extra 11 · Aldol condensation (Q39)
Which of the following will not undergo aldol condensation?
Show answer
Answer: The compound with no α-hydrogen

Aldol needs an α-H (H on the carbon next to C=O) to form the enolate. No α-H → no aldol, e.g. HCHO (formaldehyde), C₆H₅CHO (benzaldehyde), (CH₃)₃C–CHO. (The group only remembered the idea, not the options.)

Question 1
Which of the following cycloalkanes has the highest angle strain?
  • A) cycloheptane
  • B) cyclohexane
  • C) cyclopentane
  • D) cyclobutane
  • E) cyclopropane
Show answer
Answer: E — cyclopropane

Ring angle 60° vs 109.5° → biggest deviation → highest angle strain.

Question 2
What is the number of polar bonds in this compound?
  • A) 1
  • B) 2
  • C) 3
  • D) 4
  • E) 5
Show answer
Answer: B — 2

The two C–O bonds are polar; C–C and C–H are non-polar.

Question 3
What is A in the following reaction?
  • A) o-nitrophenol
  • B) p-nitrophenol
  • C) o-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol
  • D) 3,4,5-trinitrophenol
  • E) 2,4,6-trinitrophenol
Show answer
Answer: E — 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid)

OH is an o/p director; 3 HNO₃ add NO₂ at both ortho and the para positions → 2,4,6.

Question 4
Which of the following structures represents di-isopropyl ether?
Show answer
Answer: A — A

Isopropyl–O–isopropyl: each side is CH(CH₃)₂ (two branches).

Question 5
Which of the following structures best represents a pair of enantiomers?
  • A) i, ii
  • B) i, iii
  • C) ii, iii
  • D) ii, iv
Show answer
Answer: D — ii, iv

ii and iv are the two trans-1,3-cyclohexanediols (mirror images). i and iii are cis = the same meso compound.

Question 6
What is the product of the following reaction?
  • A) Propanoic acid
  • B) Propanal
  • C) Propanamine
  • D) Propanol
  • E) Propanone
Show answer
Answer: B — Propanal

PCC is a mild oxidant: 1° alcohol → aldehyde (stops there, no acid).

Question 7
Which of the following compounds CAN NOT form geometric isomers?
  • A) 2-methyl-3-hexene
  • B) 2-pentene
  • C) 3-hexene
  • D) 2-methyl-2-hexene
Show answer
Answer: D — 2-methyl-2-hexene

C2 carries two identical CH₃ groups → no cis/trans.

Question 8
In the following structure, how many chiral carbons and number of stereoisomers can form, respectively?
  • A) 2 and 4
  • B) 3 and 8
  • C) 3 and 6
  • D) 4 and 16
  • E) 5 and 32
Show answer
Answer: A — 2 and 4

Only the two ring carbons of the β-lactam (wedge/dash) are stereocentres → 2² = 4.

Question 9
Which of the following groups are equatorial and above the plane?
  • A) CN and Cl
  • B) C₂H₅ and SCH₃
  • C) C₂H₅ and Br
  • D) Br and SCH₃
Show answer
Answer: D — Br and SCH₃

Answer key: D. Equatorial bonds point outwards (roughly in the ring plane); look for the ones tilted upward.

Question 10
Alcohols have higher boiling points than ethers because –OH can form ……
  • A) dipole–dipole bonds
  • B) hydrogen bonds
  • C) van der Waals bonds
  • D) ionic bonds
Show answer
Answer: B — hydrogen bonds

O–H donates H-bonds to other alcohol molecules; ethers cannot.

Question 11
What is the product of the reaction of (CH₃)₂NH with acetone (CH₃COCH₃)?
  • A) diazonium salt
  • B) enamine
  • C) ammonia
  • D) imine
  • E) Schiff’s base
Show answer
Answer: B — enamine

2° amine + aldehyde/ketone → enamine (1° amine → imine/Schiff base).

Question 12
Which of the following are meso compounds?
  • A) i & ii
  • B) i & iii
  • C) ii & iii
  • D) iii & iv
  • E) i & ii & iii
Show answer
Answer: C — ii & iii

Same groups top and bottom + same groups on the same side → internal mirror plane → meso.

Question 13
What is the name of the following structure?
Show answer
Answer: 2,5-dichlorohex-5-en-3-ol

OH gets the lowest number (C3, numbering from the CH₃ end); C=C at C5; Cl at C2 and C5.

Question 14
What is the product of the following reaction?
  • A) Phenol + ethyl bromide
  • B) Bromobenzene + ethanol
  • C) Bromobenzene + ethyl bromide
  • D) Phenol + ethanol
Show answer
Answer: A — Phenol + ethyl bromide

The aryl–O bond (sp² C) is not cleaved; Br attacks the ethyl group.

Question 15
What is the name of the following structure?
Show answer
Answer: 4-ethyl-5,5-dimethyl-2-heptene

Longest chain containing C=C = 7 C; number from the end nearest C=C (C2); ethyl at C4, two methyls at C5.

Question 16
Which of the following has the highest boiling point?
Show answer
Answer: B — B (1° amine, butylamine)

1° amine has two N–H → most H-bonding here; aldehyde, 3° amine and alkane cannot H-bond to themselves; 2° amine has one N–H.

Question 17
The resolution of the racemic mixture of naproxen shown below can be achieved by:
  • A) Reacting the racemic mixture directly with an enzyme
  • B) Separation on normal silica gel column chromatography
  • C) Converting the acid to ester, then hydrolysing the ester with esterase to pure S and R enantiomer
  • D) Converting the acid to ester, reducing the ester to the alcohol and hydrolysing with esterase to give pure enantiomer

Answer: C — Ester → esterase hydrolysis

The enzyme (esterase) hydrolyses only one enantiomer of the ester → the two can be separated.

Question 18
What is the product of the following reaction?
Show answer
Answer: Bromocyclohexane + ethyl bromide

2 equiv HBr: first cleavage gives an alcohol + alkyl bromide, the second HBr turns the alcohol into a bromide too (+ H₂O).

Question 19
Which of the following is the correct structure for 1-ethynyl-2-isopropylcyclohexane?
Show answer
Answer: A — A

Ethynyl (–C≡CH) on C1 and isopropyl on the next ring carbon (C2).

Question 20
Which of the following is the most acidic compound?
Show answer
Answer: B — B (2,4-dinitrophenol)

Two NO₂ groups (o/p, strong EWG) stabilise the phenoxide most. Alcohols (E) are the least acidic.

Question 21
Which of the following is the least basic compound?
  • A) CH₃CH₂NH₂
  • B) CH₃CONH₂
  • C) CH₃CONHCOCH₃
Show answer
Answer: C — CH₃CONHCOCH₃

Question 22
What is the product of this reaction?
Show answer
Answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂NH₂ (propylamine)

Question 23
What is the type of the following reaction?
  • A) Electrophilic addition
  • B) E1
  • C) E2
  • D) Nucleophilic substitution SN1
  • E) Nucleophilic substitution SN2
Show answer
Answer: D — SN1

tert-Butanol + HBr: OH is protonated, leaves as H₂O → stable 3° carbocation → Br⁻ attacks.

Question 24
Which of the following is the most basic?
Show answer
Answer: B — B (2,4,6-trimethylaniline)

Answer key: B — three CH₃ (electron-donating) make it more basic than aniline. Note: in reality NH₃ (pKb 4.75) is a stronger base than any aniline.

Question 25
What is the product of the following reaction?
Show answer
Answer: A — A

Basic medium (CH₃O⁻) → SN2 attack at the less hindered epoxide carbon (CH₂) → OCH₃ on CH₂, OH on the C(CH₃)₂.
